resources.string: Pay without internet
Pay without internet
Scan a UPI QR code. Needs only phone signal.
Pay by UPI when there\'s no internet

No internet, but a bar of phone signal? You can still pay by UPI on Airtel, Vi, BSNL and MTNL. Hopline reads the QR code, then hands over to *99# — your bank\'s own service, which runs on plain phone signal.
Scan a QR code
Point at the UPI QR code
Hopline needs the camera to scan a QR code. You can type the UPI ID instead.
Hopline can\'t use the camera
To scan a QR code, allow the camera for Hopline in Settings. Or type the UPI ID instead — most shops print it under their code.
Type a UPI ID
UPI ID, like name@bank
Next
That doesn\'t look like a UPI ID. It should look like name@bank.
That\'s a phone number. Ask for their UPI ID — it looks like name@bank.
You have internet right now, so your usual UPI app will be quicker. This way is for when you don\'t.
No phone signal right now. *99# needs ordinary signal — try again when you have a bar.
This phone\'s SIM looks like Jio, and *99# doesn\'t work on Jio. If your bank has the number of another SIM in this phone, choose that SIM when the Phone app opens.

Good to know
Up to ₹5,000 at a time. Your bank may allow less in a day.
Works on Airtel, Vi, BSNL and MTNL. Not on Jio.
Call from the SIM whose number your bank has.
Works best with a shop\'s printed QR code or a person\'s UPI ID. A code made for one bill — on a card machine or a website — may not work.
Hopline never sees your UPI PIN. You type it into your phone company\'s own box.
Never used *99#? Set it up once. You\'ll need your debit card, and no internet.
Set up *99#

This code was made for one bill. Paying it this way may fail, or the shop may not see which bill you paid. If you can, ask for the shop\'s printed QR code or its UPI ID.

Only an amount in figures can go here, like 250 or 1250.50.
What happens next
Hopline copies the UPI ID and opens the Phone app with *99*1*3# typed in. Press call — on the SIM your bank has.
A box asks for the UPI ID. Press and hold inside it, then tap Paste.
Your bank shows a name. If it\'s who you mean to pay, type the amount: %1$s
Your bank shows a name. If it\'s who you mean to pay, type the amount.
When it asks for a remark, send 1 to skip it.
Type your UPI PIN and send. The PIN shows as you type, so keep the screen to yourself.
Step %1$s. %2$s
Hopline never sees or asks for your PIN.
Copy UPI ID and open *99#
UPI ID
UPI ID copied
Did it go through?
Hopline can\'t see inside the *99# box. The message your bank showed, and its SMS, are your proof.
%1$s to %2$s
Yes, it\'s paid

What went wrong?
“Connection problem or invalid MMI code” — that SIM can\'t reach *99#. It may be Jio, or have no signal. Try your other SIM.
It asked for your language or your bank — *99# isn\'t set up on that number yet. Set it up, then pay again.
It showed a menu instead of asking for the UPI ID — choose Send Money, then UPI ID.
It said the UPI ID is wrong — check it pasted in full; some networks cut it short at the @. You can type it by hand: %1$s
It said declined or failed — a code made for one bill often can\'t be paid this way, and your bank may have reached its limit for the day.
Not sure if the money left? Don\'t pay twice. Open *99#, choose Transactions, and look.
